result.title: AuDiR: Diagnosing Audio Reasoning with Rule and Percept Interventions
result.summary: Answer accuracy alone does not distinguish failures in acoustic perception, rule knowledge, and rule application. AuDiR (Audio Diagnostic Reasoning) examines these distinctions through controlled input interventions. Each item contains an audio clip, a multiple-choice question, a task-general rule, and a textual description of the acoustic observations needed to answer. Three conditions progressively supply the rule and observations; a fourth removes the audio while retaining the question and rule. The first correct diagnostic condition assigns an operational response label, without identifying a unique internal cause. The current benchmark contains 201 items in 18 families drawn from 9 sources, with answer references documented separately from percept extraction. In a preliminary evaluation of Gemini-3.8-flash, accuracy is 29.3% without supplied information, 31.3% with the rule, and 98.5% with the observations also supplied. No-audio accuracy is 23.9%, with a confidence interval containing the 25.0% chance rate. A family-level knowledge probe associates incomplete rule recall with larger gains from rule provision. These results show the benefit of supplying acoustic observations as text, while incomplete validation, possible recognition shortcuts, and non-monotonic responses limit stronger failure-attribution claims.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建音频诊断基准 AuDiR（201 题、18 个任务族），通过逐步提供任务规则与声学观测文本、以及移除音频的四类输入条件，尝试区分声学感知、规则知识与规则应用的失败，并给出 Gemini-3.8-flash 的初步评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 把声学观测改以文本提供时准确率由 31.3% 升至 98.5%，与 LVR 关注的「视觉证据经文本旁路供给」及感知缺失和信息坍缩问题同构，其干预条件与标签可供核查能否迁移到分离视觉 latent 内容的贡献。
